correctness.rationale: Direct modal semantics reduces a local failure to simultaneous two-colouring of all successor neighborhoods. Under maximum outdegree two, at most two binary constraints are always splittable unless a dead-end or singleton successor forces validity; globally dead ends are excluded. The unique singleton-set row decomposition yields the exact integer count. Elementary binomial estimates around n/W_0(n) give the logarithmic asymptotic. The six-world triangle obstruction verifies sharpness. Independent exhaustive finite checks tested every frame and valuation through four worlds, corroborating but not replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 26 in van Benthem–ten Cate–Yang proves unrestricted finite-frame coNP-completeness through set splitting, not a bounded-outdegree labelled classification, its exact count, rarity asymptotic, or sharp degree-three obstruction. Chen–Ma proves a singleton-or-terminal condition on weakly transitive frames; its hypothesis cannot be omitted to cover arbitrary degree-two frames. A close OEIS initial sequence coincidence separates at n=5. Semantic searches of published-finding corpus and public literature did not identify a logically dominating result; older unidentified equivalent coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: The degree-two structural implication may have appeared as an unpublished or differently named special case of bounded-branching modal correspondence.
Older finite Kripke frame enumeration or marked-digraph tables under different terminology might contain the same binomial formula even if no indexed match was located.
One cannot use absence of a published-finding corpus search hit as independent novelty certification.

value.rationale: The source coNP-completeness result motivates an exact tractable boundary for finite modal frames. Here the entire nontrivial degree-two family is characterized without transitivity, enumerated exactly for all orders, and shown asymptotically vanishing among bounded-degree relations; a concrete degree-three obstruction establishes the scope boundary. This is a natural complete finite-model enumeration, not a renaming or a tiny arbitrary numerical improvement.
